responsibility: Implements forward copy propagation on hard registers after allocation/reload. It tracks equivalence classes of hard registers, replaces uses with older equivalent hard registers when legal for operands, addresses, or memory references, updates and defers debug-insn substitutions carefully, and iterates over changed basic blocks to reduce false dependencies and clean up suboptimal reload decisions. The pass’s main purpose is to expose more scheduling freedom and remove unnecessary hard-register copies in RTL.
same_name_distinction: This is the full hard-register copy-propagation pass implementation, including value tracking, debug-insn handling, and the RTL pass driver. The same-stem header gcc/regcprop.h only publishes a small helper entry point for running block-local propagation logic from nearby code.
